blocks.en_text: In 2020, I had a baby.
blocks.zh_text: 2020年，我生了个孩子。

blocks.en_text: Two days later...
blocks.zh_text: 两天后……

blocks.en_text: Thank you.
blocks.zh_text: 谢谢。

blocks.en_text: Two days later, COVID shut down the world,
blocks.zh_text: 两天后，新冠疫情让整个世界停摆了，

blocks.en_text: and I was as worried and as grocery-wiping as anyone.
blocks.zh_text: 我和大家一样焦虑，一样会去擦购物袋。

blocks.en_text: But truthfully, quarantine worked out pretty well for maternity leave.
blocks.zh_text: 但说实话，隔离对休产假来说还挺不错的。

blocks.en_text: I was tethered to a very hungry little boy.
blocks.zh_text: 我被拴在一个特别能吃的小男孩身边。

blocks.en_text: Shockingly hungry. He ate all the time.
blocks.zh_text: 饿得惊人。他一直在吃。

blocks.en_text: Now, I already had one full time job: seeing patients as a psychiatrist.
blocks.zh_text: 要知道，我本来就有一份全职工作：当精神科医生看病人。

blocks.en_text: In that world, I would be hurriedly switching back and forth
blocks.zh_text: 在那个世界里，我得匆匆忙忙地来回切换，

blocks.en_text: between medication, therapy, strategy, empathy, phone calls, admin, supervision.
blocks.zh_text: 在开药、治疗、策略、共情、打电话、行政事务、督导之间。

blocks.en_text: In my COVID mom life,
blocks.zh_text: 而在我的疫情妈妈生活里，

blocks.en_text: I was a human milk farm bound to the couch.
blocks.zh_text: 我就是一台被绑在沙发上的产奶机。

blocks.en_text: So how did I pass my time? Thank you so much for asking.
blocks.zh_text: 那我是怎么打发时间的呢？谢谢你问这个问题。

blocks.en_text: I watched Love Island.
blocks.zh_text: 我在看《爱情岛》。

blocks.en_text: Each season more salacious than the last.
blocks.zh_text: 每一季都比上一季更劲爆。

blocks.en_text: And for those of you who aren’t familiar with this UK dating show,
blocks.zh_text: 对于那些不熟悉这档英国相亲节目的人，

blocks.en_text: it’s trash.
blocks.zh_text: 它就是垃圾。

blocks.en_text: But it will eat up hours of your life
blocks.zh_text: 但它会吞掉你人生中好几个小时，

blocks.en_text: because there is backbiting and twists and turns and British slang.
blocks.zh_text: 因为里面有背后捅刀、有反转、还有英国俚语。

blocks.en_text: And it’s highly recommended.
blocks.zh_text: 而且强烈推荐。

blocks.en_text: I was obsessed.
blocks.zh_text: 我迷上了。

blocks.en_text: But then something weird happened.
blocks.zh_text: 但后来发生了件怪事。

blocks.en_text: My Hulu stopped working, which is actually not even true.
blocks.zh_text: 我的Hulu用不了了，其实也不是真的用不了。

blocks.en_text: The account that I’d been mooching off of reset their password
blocks.zh_text: 是我一直蹭用的那个账号重置了密码，

blocks.en_text: so I couldn’t get in.
blocks.zh_text: 所以我登不进去了。

blocks.en_text: Okay.
blocks.zh_text: 好吧。

blocks.en_text: And I probably could have gotten my own, but that would have required focus.
blocks.zh_text: 我大概也能自己开一个，但那需要专注。

blocks.en_text: Focus and energy.
blocks.zh_text: 专注和精力。

blocks.en_text: So here I was,
blocks.zh_text: 于是我就这样，

blocks.en_text: six to eight hours of a day of nursing or pumping
blocks.zh_text: 一天六到八个小时都在喂奶或泵奶，

blocks.en_text: with no Love Island.
blocks.zh_text: 却没有《爱情岛》可看。

blocks.en_text: Okay.
blocks.zh_text: 好吧。

blocks.en_text: I was so addicted to the show
blocks.zh_text: 我对这节目太上瘾了，

blocks.en_text: that I didn’t even know where to start replacing that kind of dopamine hit.
blocks.zh_text: 以至于我根本不知道该从哪儿开始替代那种多巴胺快感。

blocks.en_text: So I didn’t.
blocks.zh_text: 所以我干脆没找。

blocks.en_text: I just sat there for hours and I didn’t do anything in particular.
blocks.zh_text: 我就那么一坐好几个小时，什么特别的事也不做。

blocks.en_text: I just remember being profoundly and existentially bored.
blocks.zh_text: 我只记得自己无聊到了极点，无聊到怀疑人生。

blocks.en_text: And that continued for days until something weirder happened.
blocks.zh_text: 这样持续了好几天，直到更奇怪的事发生了。

blocks.en_text: My brain, which had been reduced to absolute oatmeal throughout this time,
blocks.zh_text: 我的大脑，这段时间里已经退化成一团浆糊，

blocks.en_text: seemed to reset.
blocks.zh_text: 似乎重启了。

blocks.en_text: I started thinking about creative ways to spend my time.
blocks.zh_text: 我开始琢磨怎么有创意地打发时间。

blocks.en_text: I started brainstorming how to get more people
blocks.zh_text: 我开始头脑风暴，想办法让更多人

blocks.en_text: better access to good, sound information on mental health care.
blocks.zh_text: 更容易获得可靠、正确的心理健康护理信息。

blocks.en_text: I started to research, imagine,
blocks.zh_text: 我开始做研究、展开想象，

blocks.en_text: then create educational content around that.
blocks.zh_text: 然后围绕这些制作教育内容。

blocks.en_text: I put some of those videos online
blocks.zh_text: 我把其中一些视频发到了网上，

blocks.en_text: and before I knew it, I had over a million followers across platforms.
blocks.zh_text: 不知不觉间，我在各个平台上就有了超过一百万的粉丝。

blocks.en_text: Because of those videos, I was offered a book deal.
blocks.zh_text: 因为那些视频，我拿到了一份出书合同。

blocks.en_text: I was able to develop an ADHD management app.
blocks.zh_text: 我得以开发出一款ADHD管理应用。

blocks.en_text: I was asked by the vice president and the surgeon general
blocks.zh_text: 副总统和卫生总监邀请我

blocks.en_text: to speak about burnout.
blocks.zh_text: 去讲一讲职业倦怠。

blocks.en_text: And all of those things happened
blocks.zh_text: 而所有这些事情的发生

blocks.en_text: because my Hulu stopped working.
blocks.zh_text: 都是因为我的Hulu不工作了。

blocks.en_text: All of those things happened
blocks.zh_text: 所有这些事情的发生

blocks.en_text: because I was stuck to the couch with a dull routine.
blocks.zh_text: 都是因为我被无聊的日常困在沙发上。

blocks.en_text: All of that happened because I was bored.
blocks.zh_text: 这一切的发生都是因为我无聊了。

blocks.en_text: Now, most of my content and educational research is about ADHD.
blocks.zh_text: 现在，我的大部分内容和教育研究都是关于ADHD的。

blocks.en_text: I have it and I treat it.
blocks.zh_text: 我自己有ADHD，我也治疗它。

blocks.en_text: So I spent a lot of my time focusing on focus.
blocks.zh_text: 所以我花了很多时间专注于“专注”这件事。

blocks.en_text: And I started to wonder,
blocks.zh_text: 我开始琢磨，

blocks.en_text: why was there such a seismic shift in my focus?
blocks.zh_text: 为什么我的专注力会发生这么大的转变？

blocks.en_text: And I’ll tell you,
blocks.zh_text: 我来告诉你，

blocks.en_text: it’s because I allowed myself to be bored.
blocks.zh_text: 是因为我允许自己感到无聊。

blocks.en_text: The true secret to dialing in
blocks.zh_text: 真正能让你进入状态的秘诀

blocks.en_text: is being able to space out.
blocks.zh_text: 是能够放空发呆。

blocks.en_text: Your brain is a very busy place.
blocks.zh_text: 你的大脑是个非常忙碌的地方。

blocks.en_text: Parts of it are working even when you think they aren’t.
blocks.zh_text: 即使你以为某些部分没在工作，它们其实也在运转。

blocks.en_text: And you probably heard that myth that you only use 10% of your brain.
blocks.zh_text: 你可能听过那个说法，说你只用了大脑的10%。

blocks.en_text: That’s not true. You actually use all of it.
blocks.zh_text: 那不是真的。你其实用到了全部。

blocks.en_text: Even when you’re sleeping, your brain is always active.
blocks.zh_text: 即使在你睡觉的时候，你的大脑也一直很活跃。

blocks.en_text: So when you’re awake, alert, focused on a task,
blocks.zh_text: 所以当你醒着、警觉、专注于一项任务时，

blocks.en_text: you’re being ripped in a million different directions by distractions.
blocks.zh_text: 各种干扰正把你撕扯向无数个不同的方向。

blocks.en_text: And that’s not even an ADHD-specific thing.
blocks.zh_text: 这甚至不是ADHD特有的现象。

blocks.en_text: That’s a human-in-this-modern-world thing.
blocks.zh_text: 这是现代世界里作为人的普遍现象。

blocks.en_text: So when you attempt to multitask,
blocks.zh_text: 所以当你试图同时做多件事时，

blocks.en_text: you’re not actually doing more than one activity at a time.
blocks.zh_text: 你其实并不是真的在同时做一件以上的事。

blocks.en_text: Instead, you’re rapidly shifting your focus from one thing to another,
blocks.zh_text: 你是在快速地把注意力从一件事切换到另一件事，

blocks.en_text: using up oxygenated glucose in the brain,
blocks.zh_text: 消耗着大脑里的含氧葡萄糖，

blocks.en_text: which is exactly the fuel you need when you're trying to focus.
blocks.zh_text: 而这恰恰是你想要专注时所需的燃料。

blocks.en_text: So here you are, burning through your resources,
blocks.zh_text: 于是你就在这儿，把自己的资源烧个精光，

blocks.en_text: and it's even harder to stay on task for a prolonged period of time.
blocks.zh_text: 想要长时间保持专注就更难了。

blocks.en_text: So you jump from task to task even more,
blocks.zh_text: 于是你更频繁地从一项任务跳到另一项任务，

blocks.en_text: and you use up more glucose, and you keep jumping,
blocks.zh_text: 消耗更多葡萄糖，然后继续跳，

blocks.en_text: and it goes on and on,
blocks.zh_text: 如此反复不停，

blocks.en_text: and you get stuck on this vicious cycle of brain fatigue.
blocks.zh_text: 你就陷进了大脑疲劳的恶性循环。

blocks.en_text: And it’s exhausting.
blocks.zh_text: 这让人精疲力竭。

blocks.en_text: So how do we exit that loop?
blocks.zh_text: 那我们怎么跳出这个循环呢？

blocks.en_text: When you allow your brain to quiet down,
blocks.zh_text: 当你让大脑安静下来时，

blocks.en_text: you activate lesser-known neural pathways called the default mode network.
blocks.zh_text: 你会激活一些鲜为人知的神经通路，叫做默认模式网络。

blocks.en_text: And I would describe that neurologically, but it's a relatively recent concept.
blocks.zh_text: 我本可以从神经学角度来描述它，但它是个相对较新的概念。

blocks.en_text: There’s not a complete consensus
blocks.zh_text: 目前还没有完全的共识

blocks.en_text: on all the brain regions included in the definition of it.
blocks.zh_text: 来确定它定义中到底包含哪些脑区。

blocks.en_text: But what we do know is that these are the areas of the brain
blocks.zh_text: 但我们知道的是，这些是大脑中的区域

blocks.en_text: that are active when your brain is at wakeful rest,
blocks.zh_text: 它们在你大脑处于清醒休息状态时是活跃的，

blocks.en_text: like daydreaming.
blocks.zh_text: 比如做白日梦的时候。

blocks.en_text: So when you're spacing out in the shower,
blocks.zh_text: 所以当你在洗澡时走神，

blocks.en_text: when you’re sitting in the car on a long, boring drive,
blocks.zh_text: 当你坐在车里经历一段漫长无聊的驾驶，

blocks.en_text: when you’re fused to a breast pump,
blocks.zh_text: 当你被吸奶器拴住动弹不得时，

blocks.en_text: that’s when your default mode engages,
blocks.zh_text: 那就是你的默认模式启动的时候，

blocks.en_text: When your brain has nothing better to do,
blocks.zh_text: 当你大脑无事可做时，

blocks.en_text: you dip into these emotional and memory centers of the brain.
blocks.zh_text: 你就会潜入大脑中这些情绪和记忆中心。

blocks.en_text: And the result is that you get to access forgotten memories,
blocks.zh_text: 结果就是你能接触到被遗忘的记忆，

blocks.en_text: tap into repressed emotions,
blocks.zh_text: 触及被压抑的情绪，

blocks.en_text: and problem-solve with tools not usually accessible in your toolbox.
blocks.zh_text: 并用平时工具箱里拿不到的工具来解决问题。

blocks.en_text: And this concept is especially important
blocks.zh_text: 这个概念尤其重要

blocks.en_text: to those of us who have focus issues at baseline.
blocks.zh_text: 对我们这些本来就有专注力问题的人来说。

blocks.en_text: In the neurotypical brain, the default mode network,
blocks.zh_text: 在神经典型的大脑中，默认模式网络

blocks.en_text: and the task-positive or executive network are reciprocal.
blocks.zh_text: 和任务正向网络，也就是执行网络，是此消彼长的。

blocks.en_text: As one works more, the other slows down.
blocks.zh_text: 一个运转得越多，另一个就慢下来。

blocks.en_text: For people who have focus issues, the default mode remains active
blocks.zh_text: 对于有专注力问题的人，默认模式网络会一直保持活跃

blocks.en_text: while the executive network is trying to get stuff done,
blocks.zh_text: 而执行网络正试图把事情做完，

blocks.en_text: which explains why it’s so hard to stay on task.
blocks.zh_text: 这就解释了为什么保持专注这么难。

blocks.en_text: In order to reclaim our fragmented focus
blocks.zh_text: 为了找回我们支离破碎的专注力

blocks.en_text: from an increasingly distracted world,
blocks.zh_text: 从一个越来越让人分心的世界里，

blocks.en_text: we need to be able to tap into the default mode network
blocks.zh_text: 我们需要能够调动默认模式网络

blocks.en_text: because there's magic in there.
blocks.zh_text: 因为那里有奇妙之处。

blocks.en_text: So how do we do that?
blocks.zh_text: 那我们该怎么做呢？

blocks.en_text: There’s a ton of research out there
blocks.zh_text: 有大量研究

blocks.en_text: showing how to suppress the default mode network.
blocks.zh_text: 展示了如何抑制默认模式网络。

blocks.en_text: There’s a lot of solid data showing how mindfulness, meditation, and exercise
blocks.zh_text: 有很多可靠的数据表明，正念、冥想和运动

blocks.en_text: diminish the default mode network.
blocks.zh_text: 能减弱默认模式网络。

blocks.en_text: Mindfulness, meditation, and exercise influence the way we process thoughts.
blocks.zh_text: 正念、冥想和运动会影响我们处理想法的方式。

blocks.en_text: And it does it by diminishing the default mode network.
blocks.zh_text: 而它是通过减弱默认模式网络来实现的。

blocks.en_text: You’re probably thinking, why are we diminishing it?
blocks.zh_text: 你可能会想，我们为什么要减弱它呢？

blocks.en_text: Don’t we want to use the default mode network?
blocks.zh_text: 我们不是想用默认模式网络吗？

blocks.en_text: Yes.
blocks.zh_text: 是的。

blocks.en_text: But mindfulness, meditation, and exercise serve to clean up both of our networks,
blocks.zh_text: 但正念、冥想和运动的作用是清理我们的两个网络，

blocks.en_text: reorganizing the mind.
blocks.zh_text: 重新整理心智。

blocks.en_text: So when we’re focusing, we’re focusing. And when we're not, we're not.
blocks.zh_text: 这样当我们专注时，我们就专注。当我们不专注时，我们就不专注。

blocks.en_text: And this is really important to those of us tho have
blocks.zh_text: 这对我们这些

blocks.en_text: both networks firing at the same time.
blocks.zh_text: 两个网络同时运转的人来说非常重要。

blocks.en_text: But I'm not here to talk about meditation, and I'm not here to talk about exercise.
blocks.zh_text: 但我来这里不是谈冥想的，也不是谈运动的。

blocks.en_text: Instead,
blocks.zh_text: 相反，

blocks.en_text: I’m here to encourage you
blocks.zh_text: 我来这里是想鼓励你们

blocks.en_text: to exercise mindlessness
blocks.zh_text: 练习“无心”

blocks.en_text: as a way to unlock your most creative, most productive self
blocks.zh_text: 以此释放你最有创造力、最高效的自己

blocks.en_text: by activating the default mode network.
blocks.zh_text: 通过激活默认模式网络。

blocks.en_text: Okay, so Einstein...
blocks.zh_text: 好，那么爱因斯坦……

blocks.en_text: Einstein was a daydreamer.
blocks.zh_text: 爱因斯坦是个爱做白日梦的人。

blocks.en_text: He recommended it. He actively participated in it.
blocks.zh_text: 他推荐了它。他积极地参与其中。

blocks.en_text: Why?
blocks.zh_text: 为什么？

blocks.en_text: Because when the default mode network is active,
blocks.zh_text: 因为当默认模式网络活跃时，

blocks.en_text: creativity and problem-solving are optimized.
blocks.zh_text: 创造力和解决问题的能力会达到最佳状态。

blocks.en_text: When the default mode network is actively firing,
blocks.zh_text: 当默认模式网络积极运作时，

blocks.en_text: you naturally demote your executive network.
blocks.zh_text: 你会自然而然地降低执行网络的优先级。

blocks.en_text: Give it some time off between tasks.
blocks.zh_text: 在任务之间给它一些休息时间。

blocks.en_text: This is when creativity flourishes.
blocks.zh_text: 这正是创造力蓬勃发展的时刻。

blocks.en_text: So when you return to problem-solving,
blocks.zh_text: 所以当你重新回到解决问题时，

blocks.en_text: you’ve actually reset your executive network.
blocks.zh_text: 你实际上已经重置了你的执行网络。

blocks.en_text: And sometimes even given it new ideas to sort through and select from.
blocks.zh_text: 有时甚至给了它新的想法去梳理和挑选。

blocks.en_text: And I get it,
blocks.zh_text: 我明白，

blocks.en_text: not a lot of people encourage daydreaming.
blocks.zh_text: 没有多少人鼓励做白日梦。

blocks.en_text: Usually when we’re in it, we try to snap out of it
blocks.zh_text: 通常当我们沉浸其中时，我们会试图赶紧摆脱它，

blocks.en_text: because we’re busy.
blocks.zh_text: 因为我们很忙。

blocks.en_text: But clearly there’s value in it. Our brains are literally trying to reset.
blocks.zh_text: 但显然它是有价值的。我们的大脑真的在试图重置。

blocks.en_text: So how do we purposefully be mindless?
blocks.zh_text: 那么，我们如何有目的地放空呢？

blocks.en_text: It seems like a paradox, right?
blocks.zh_text: 这看起来像个悖论，对吧？

blocks.en_text: We can trigger these mind-wandering breaks
blocks.zh_text: 我们可以触发这些走神休息，

blocks.en_text: with a concept that I call brain babbling.
blocks.zh_text: 用一个我称之为“大脑咿呀”的概念。

blocks.en_text: Brain babbling
blocks.zh_text: 大脑咿呀

blocks.en_text: is the expression of the contents of your consciousness without censorship
blocks.zh_text: 就是不加审查地表达你意识中的内容，

blocks.en_text: as a means of activating and stimulating your unconscious.
blocks.zh_text: 以此作为激活和刺激你潜意识的手段。

blocks.en_text: So the next time you feel stuck, I want you to try this.
blocks.zh_text: 所以下次你感到卡住的时候，我想让你试试这个。

blocks.en_text: Look around you and grab hold of something you see.
blocks.zh_text: 环顾四周，抓住你看到的某样东西。

blocks.en_text: I’m going to give you an example.
blocks.zh_text: 我给你们举个例子。

blocks.en_text: I’ll give you a phone-related example because I’m always around my phone.
blocks.zh_text: 我举一个和手机有关的例子，因为我总是手机不离身。

blocks.en_text: So, phone...
blocks.zh_text: 那么，手机……

blocks.en_text: I’m going to start with the word “cell.”
blocks.zh_text: 我从“cell”这个词开始。

blocks.en_text: Cell. Genetics. DNA. Evolution. Caveman.
blocks.zh_text: Cell。遗传学。DNA。进化。穴居人。

blocks.en_text: Cave painting. Handprint. Fingerprint.
blocks.zh_text: 洞穴壁画。手印。指纹。

blocks.en_text: Criminal. Smooth criminal. Michael Jackson.
blocks.zh_text: 罪犯。犯罪高手。迈克尔·杰克逊。

blocks.en_text: Moon --
blocks.zh_text: 月亮——

blocks.en_text: Moonwalk.
blocks.zh_text: 太空步。

blocks.en_text: Moon --
blocks.zh_text: 月亮——

blocks.en_text: Can you guys imagine if I had fallen there?
blocks.zh_text: 你们能想象如果我刚才在那儿摔倒了吗？

blocks.en_text: I would have had to explain to everybody
blocks.zh_text: 我就得向所有人解释

blocks.en_text: that I fell while attempting to moonwalk during a Ted talk.
blocks.zh_text: 我在TED演讲中尝试走太空步时摔倒了。

blocks.en_text: Moonwalk.
blocks.zh_text: 太空步。

blocks.en_text: You can see how far we’ve come from “cell” to “moonwalk.”
blocks.zh_text: 你们可以看到我们从“cell”到“moonwalk”走了多远。

blocks.en_text: I’ll give you another example. Maybe let’s do “phone” this time.
blocks.zh_text: 我再给你们举个例子。这次也许用“phone”吧。

blocks.en_text: Phone.
blocks.zh_text: 手机。

blocks.en_text: Alexander Graham Bell. Graham cracker.
blocks.zh_text: 亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔。全麦饼干。

blocks.en_text: S’mores. Campfire. Smokey the Bear.
blocks.zh_text: 棉花糖夹心饼干。篝火。护林熊斯莫基。

blocks.en_text: Yellowstone Park. Geysers. Steam.
blocks.zh_text: 黄石公园。间歇泉。蒸汽。

blocks.en_text: Steamy Romance.
blocks.zh_text: 情色浪漫小说。

blocks.en_text: Love Island.
blocks.zh_text: 《爱情岛》。

blocks.en_text: Because that’s just been imprinted in my brain now.
blocks.zh_text: 因为这个现在已经印在我脑子里了。

blocks.en_text: The point is, you can start from anywhere.
blocks.zh_text: 关键是，你可以从任何地方开始。

blocks.en_text: You could pick anything you want
blocks.zh_text: 你可以随便挑任何你想要的东西，

blocks.en_text: and you just let your associations run free.
blocks.zh_text: 然后让你的联想自由驰骋。

blocks.en_text: We don’t have to stop at a chain of words. If a memory comes up, let it play.
blocks.zh_text: 我们不必停留在词语的链条上。如果浮现出一段记忆，就让它展开。

blocks.en_text: It’s this imaginative fluidity that’s key.
blocks.zh_text: 这种想象的流动性才是关键。

blocks.en_text: Because when you return to whatever it is you were doing before,
blocks.zh_text: 因为当你回到之前在做的事情时，

blocks.en_text: you’re likely going to be more focused.
blocks.zh_text: 你很可能会更加专注。

blocks.en_text: Because you have indulged that default mode network
blocks.zh_text: 因为你纵容了那个默认模式网络

blocks.en_text: and restored your executive network.
blocks.zh_text: 并恢复了你大脑的执行网络。

blocks.en_text: Our brains need these breaks.
blocks.zh_text: 我们的大脑需要这些休息。

blocks.en_text: It’s what moves the needle from surviving to thriving.
blocks.zh_text: 正是它让我们从勉强生存走向蓬勃发展。

blocks.en_text: We evolved as creatures with complex minds,
blocks.zh_text: 我们进化成了拥有复杂心智的生物，

blocks.en_text: alert to danger,
blocks.zh_text: 对危险保持警觉，

blocks.en_text: constantly predicting and solving problems.
blocks.zh_text: 不断预测和解决问题。

blocks.en_text: But we used to get bored also.
blocks.zh_text: 但我们也曾经会感到无聊。

blocks.en_text: And now we've developed this civilization
blocks.zh_text: 而现在我们发展出了这样的文明，

blocks.en_text: that seems designed to prevent boredom at all costs.
blocks.zh_text: 它似乎就是为了不惜一切代价防止无聊而设计的。

blocks.en_text: Endless distraction available 24-7.
blocks.zh_text: 无穷无尽的干扰全天候随时可得。

blocks.en_text: But what is that doing to us?
blocks.zh_text: 但这正在对我们做什么呢？

blocks.en_text: The key idea here is finding a way to utilize mindlessness
blocks.zh_text: 这里的关键思路是找到一种方法，利用无意识状态

blocks.en_text: as a way of becoming more mindful.
blocks.zh_text: 来让自己变得更有正念。

blocks.en_text: And I don’t want you to be mindless all the time.
blocks.zh_text: 我并不是想让你一直处于无意识状态。

blocks.en_text: Nobody wants that.
blocks.zh_text: 没人想要那样。

blocks.en_text: We don’t want to be spacing out all the time.
blocks.zh_text: 我们不想一直走神发呆。

blocks.en_text: We just want to be able to focus when we want to focus.
blocks.zh_text: 我们只是希望在想专注的时候能够专注。

blocks.en_text: And we do that by using the default mode network.
blocks.zh_text: 而我们做到这一点，靠的就是运用默认模式网络。

blocks.en_text: And remember, I got interested in this
blocks.zh_text: 记住，我对这个话题产生兴趣

blocks.en_text: because of the profound effect that being mindless had on me.
blocks.zh_text: 是因为无意识状态对我产生了深远的影响。

blocks.en_text: So many new ideas began to bubble up
blocks.zh_text: 那么多新想法开始涌现出来

blocks.en_text: once I didn’t have Adam and Zara’s love affair to distract me.
blocks.zh_text: 一旦我不再被Adam和Zara的恋情分心。

blocks.en_text: I think the trick for me, and for all of us,
blocks.zh_text: 我觉得对我来说，对我们所有人来说，诀窍

blocks.en_text: is to find space in our schedules to indulge the default mode network
blocks.zh_text: 就是在日程安排中留出空间，纵容默认模式网络

blocks.en_text: as a way to get our whole brain to work better.
blocks.zh_text: 以此让我们整个大脑运转得更好。

blocks.en_text: Mindlessness allows us to travel to the past, the present, the future,
blocks.zh_text: 无意识状态让我们能够游走于过去、现在和未来，

blocks.en_text: untethered to what we have to do,
blocks.zh_text: 不受我们必须做的事情的束缚，

blocks.en_text: and connects us simply to being.
blocks.zh_text: 并简单地把我们与存在本身连接起来。

blocks.en_text: Doing nothing is actually doing something,
blocks.zh_text: 什么都不做其实也是在做事，

blocks.en_text: and it’s probably doing something more than what you think,
blocks.zh_text: 而且它做的事可能比你以为的更多，

blocks.en_text: because this is generally when we find those breakthrough moments
blocks.zh_text: 因为这通常正是我们找到那些突破性时刻的时候

blocks.en_text: that feel like strokes of genius.
blocks.zh_text: 那些感觉像是天才灵感的时刻。

blocks.en_text: Because if we can access those parts of the brain,
blocks.zh_text: 因为如果我们能触及大脑的那些部分，

blocks.en_text: we have a unique opportunity to connect the two parts of ourselves.
blocks.zh_text: 我们就有了一个独特的机会，把自身的两个部分连接起来。

blocks.en_text: The focus task-performing part
blocks.zh_text: 那个专注执行任务的部分，

blocks.en_text: that helps us achieve, solve problems, make a living.
blocks.zh_text: 帮助我们取得成就、解决问题、谋生。

blocks.en_text: And the daydreamy, spacey part that restores us, makes us feel alive.
blocks.zh_text: 还有那个爱做白日梦、爱走神的部分，它让我们恢复元气，让我们感到活着。

blocks.en_text: When those two parts are really in sync,
blocks.zh_text: 当这两个部分真正同步时，

blocks.en_text: that’s a beautiful couple, I think they might just win this thing.
blocks.zh_text: 那是一对美好的搭档，我觉得它们说不定真能赢下这一局。

blocks.en_text: Thank you.
blocks.zh_text: 谢谢。
